sections.summary: Sally Kornbluth is the President of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Kornbluth stated MIT already meets or exceeds many of the compact's proposed standards, citing MIT's reinstated SAT/ACT requirement (2022), international enrollment of about 10% of undergraduates, free tuition for incoming undergraduates from families earning under $200,000, and 94% of undergraduate degrees in STEM fields. Kornbluth underscored free expression as a core MIT value, writing: "We must hear facts and opinions we don't like — and engage respectfully with those with whom we disagree." Kornbluth authored a public letter to U.S. Education Secretary Linda McMahon explaining MIT's rejection of the compact. Sally Kornbluth is president of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. As MIT president in August 2024, Kornbluth warned students that MIT would not tolerate antisemitism after orientation flyers linked to the Mapping Project, which she said promotes antisemitism. Contested account: Kornbluth stated she has repeatedly defended freedom of expression while finding the websites cited on the flyers deeply concerning. Contested account: Kornbluth testified before Congress in December about antisemitism on campus and has been embroiled in the resulting controversy since.
